original_question: Does the gene located on the short (p) arm of chromosome 6 at position 21.3, spanning base pairs 33,238,446 to 33,268,222, affect the eyes in Stickler syndrome?

final_qi.question: Does the gene located on the short (p) arm of chromosome 6 at position 21.3, spanning base pairs 33,238,446 to 33,268,222, affect the eyes in Stickler syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: The coordinates given (chromosome 6p21.3, 33,238,446-33,268,222) correspond to the COL11A2 gene. Pathogenic variants in COL11A2 cause Stickler syndrome type 3, often referred to as the “non-ocular” form of Stickler syndrome. Because COL11A2 is not expressed in the vitreous of the eye, individuals with COL11A2-related Stickler syndrome typically lack the characteristic ocular manifestations seen in other forms of the disorder (e.g., high myopia, vitreous anomalies, retinal detachment). Therefore, this gene is not considered to affect the eyes in Stickler syndrome.

final_answer.long_answer: The gene that occupies 6p21.3 from base pairs 33,238,446 to 33,268,222 is COL11A2. Pathogenic variants in COL11A2 produce the "non-ocular" (type III) form of Stickler syndrome, characterized by hearing loss and skeletal abnormalities but, by definition, no eye involvement.
